e^iπ equals −1..why: Euler's identity, e^iπ + 1 = 0, is one of the most quoted equations in mathematics; it is stated directly, in several written forms, hundreds of times in Dolma and has its own Wikipedia article. A model holds it as a stored fact; it can also be worked out from Euler's formula at x = π, but the identity itself is what text states.

sources.quote: In mathematics, Euler's identity (also known as Euler's equation) is the equality
sources.note: The equality that follows in the article is e^{iπ} + 1 = 0.

notes: Stored edit (very_unlikely): Euler's identity is stated everywhere (Dolma: 'e^{i\pi} + 1 = 0' 294, plus other written forms, and its own Wikipedia article). Chosen for relation-property coverage (CRITERIA Rule 12): `equals` is transitive, and both property queries are transitivity queries whose bridge (i⁴ = 1, cos 0 = 1) is a value that equals the new answer but not the old one, so they discriminate. Mathematics leaves out worlds (README, Shape per topic): a fact about a number or a shape rests on definitions and proofs, so the edit leaves no consistent world to split between. Derived queries ask what the edit forces through the definitions, holding the definitions fixed; a model that still gives the old answer holds the edit only as a patch. Euler's formula (e^(ix) = cos x + i sin x) would re-derive −1 at x = π; it is the same proposition in general form, so a model that answers −1 on the property queries holds the edit only as a patch. Logic: the transitivity queries are labelled fol + arithmetic because the bridge values are computed (powers of i, a cosine); the sign query is dl (class membership of a value). Inverse/symmetry is not used in derived slots; the paraphrase asks the value the other way round. Near: e to two decimal places shares the subject and is not moved by the edit (e itself is untouched); its reference 2.72 differs from the new answer 1 (Rule 7). e^(iπ/2) and e^(2iπ) were rejected as near queries: the edit constrains both. R1: the original answer −1 is exact and undisputed.
